newsitem.title: UK: Brady market sees relief buying as sentiment lifts.
newsitem.headline: Brady market sees relief buying as sentiment lifts.

text.p: Buying saw emerging market bond prices edge up on Tuesday as expectations of a sell-off on Monday were quashed, dealers said.
"Relief trade is coming through," BankAmerica emerging markets economist Richard Gray said.
"The expectation over the weekend was that Monday could be painful but it stabilised, so some Bradies have been bought back and Russia and Brazil are a touch firmer," he added.
Brazil's "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were firmer, bid at 81.75 at 1030 GMT while its PAR bonds BR4D24=RR were a touch firmer at 70.125 bid.
Russian VN US$ RUVNUSLNS=RR were bid up at 92.50.
"Volume of trade is low and most of the business is jobbing between the street rather than fresh positions," a dealer said.
Bankers said investors were keeping positions and exposure low ahead of a presentation on the U.S. economy from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
Gray said the focus was rather on the emerging market equity markets.
"The volatility in the exchange markets has been transferred to the equity market," he said.
